prompt: The planner is deployed, and somebody changes `VITE_TITLE` in the host's settings without starting a new deploy. What do readers see?

choices.text: The new title, on the next page load
choices.why: The browser has no environment to read; the value is a string in the bundle.

choices.text: The old title, until the next build
choices.why: Right. The build wrote the value into the JavaScript, and nothing reads the variable again.

choices.text: An error, because the variable no longer matches the bundle
choices.why: Nothing compares them; the bundle simply keeps its string.

choices.text: The default, `Study planner`
choices.why: The default only appears when the build saw no value.

prompt: After building with `VITE_TITLE` set, `grep -c VITE_TITLE dist/assets/*.js` prints `0`. Why?

choices.text: The build failed and wrote an empty file
choices.why: The same file contains the title's value, so the build worked.

choices.text: Minifying renamed the variable to one letter
choices.why: Minifying renames local variables; this one was replaced before that.

choices.text: Vite swapped it for the value
choices.why: Right. The bundle has the string and no trace of the variable's name.

choices.text: Variables live in `index.html`, not in the script
choices.why: This one was used in `env.ts`, so its value went into the script.

prompt: Vite exposes variables to the code under `import.meta.___`.
Match each file to when Vite reads it.

pairs.right: In every mode, and it is committed
In every mode, and git ignores it

right_distractors: Only on the host, never locally

prompt: `VITE_TITLE` is set in four places for a staging build. Order them from the one that wins to the one that loses.
items: The shell that runs the build

prompt: Which mode does `npm run build` use when no `--mode` is given?

choices.text: `development`
choices.why: That is the dev server's mode.

choices.text: `production`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `staging`
choices.why: Only when you name it.

choices.text: None, so no file is read
choices.why: `.env` and `.env.production` are read.

prompt: A value typed into a host's dashboard should beat the `.env.staging` committed in the repository. Which rule makes that happen?

choices.text: The environment beats every file
choices.why: Right. The host passes dashboard values to the build as ordinary environment variables.

choices.text: Files ending in `.local` are read last
choices.why: That orders the files among themselves; the dashboard is not a file.

choices.text: The host deletes `.env.staging` before building
choices.why: It does not need to; the environment wins anyway.

choices.text: Vite reads the dashboard through the host's API
choices.why: Vite knows nothing about hosts; it reads its environment and its files.

prompt: `SUPPORT_TOKEN` is in `.env.local`, and `main.ts` logs `import.meta.env.SUPPORT_TOKEN`. What does the bundle contain there?

choices.text: The token, because the code asked for it
choices.why: Asking is not enough; the name lacks the prefix.

choices.text: `void 0`, which is `undefined`
choices.why: Right. Without `VITE_`, the build refuses to hand the value over.

choices.text: A build error naming the variable
choices.why: A missing variable is normal to ask about, so there is no error.

choices.text: The string `SUPPORT_TOKEN`
choices.why: Neither the name nor the value is written.

prompt: Someone sets `envPrefix: ""` in `vite.config.ts` so every variable is available. What happens?

choices.text: Every variable in the shell goes into the bundle
choices.why: That is what it would mean, which is why Vite does not allow it.

choices.text: Only variables from `.env` files are exposed
choices.why: The setting does not distinguish files from the shell.

choices.text: Vite refuses to build
choices.why: Right: the error names sensitive information. The prefix can be another word, never nothing.

choices.text: Vite ignores the setting and keeps `VITE_`
choices.why: It does not ignore it; it refuses it.

prompt: Match each tool to the prefix that marks a value for the browser.
A secret token was deployed in the bundle for a week, then removed from the code and redeployed. What still has to be done?

choices.text: Nothing; the new bundle no longer has it
choices.why: Anybody who downloaded the old bundle still has it.

choices.text: Purge the CDN's cache
choices.why: That stops new copies, not the ones already downloaded.

choices.text: Minify the next build harder
choices.why: Minifying never hides a string.

choices.text: Replace the token at whatever issued it
choices.why: Right. Only that makes the leaked copies useless.

prompt: A maps service gives you a `pk_` key and an `sk_` key. Which one may go in `VITE_MAPS_KEY`?

choices.text: The `pk_` one, restricted to your domain at the service
choices.why: Right. It is meant to be public, and the domain limit protects it.

choices.text: The `sk_` one, since the prefix keeps it private
choices.why: The prefix publishes; it does not protect.

choices.text: Either, as long as the bundle is minified
choices.why: A minified string is still readable.

choices.text: Neither: no key may ever be in a front end
choices.why: Publishable keys exist precisely to be in a front end.

prompt: Which of these does a visitor to the deployed planner have access to? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Every string in the JavaScript bundle
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Every header the page sends with a request
choices.why: Right: the network panel shows them.

choices.text: Variables without the `VITE_` prefix
choices.why: Those never reach the bundle.

choices.text: A source map, if one was published
choices.why: Right; lesson 11 keeps them private.

prompt: Before `vite-env.d.ts`, `import.meta.env.VITE_TITEL` built without complaint. Why?

choices.text: TypeScript does not check `import.meta`
choices.why: It does; once the names are declared it rejects the typo.

choices.text: Vite's types accept any name by default
choices.why: Right. An index signature lets every name through.

choices.text: Vite corrects close misspellings automatically
choices.why: It does nothing of the kind; the fallback took over.

choices.text: `.env.staging` declared `VITE_TITEL` too
choices.why: It declared `VITE_TITLE`, which is why the heading lost its value.

prompt: The declarations are saved as `src/env.d.ts`, next to `src/env.ts`, and the misspelling still builds. What is wrong?

choices.text: The interfaces need an `export`
choices.why: They are global declarations; an export would not help here.

choices.text: `strictImportMetaEnv` must be `true`, not `unknown`
choices.why: Vite checks that the key exists, not its type.

choices.text: TypeScript reads it as `env.ts`'s own declarations and skips it
choices.why: Right. A `.d.ts` beside a `.ts` of the same name is ignored; `vite-env.d.ts` collides with nothing.

choices.text: `tsc` checks `.d.ts` files only with `--strict`
choices.why: Declaration files are read without that flag.

prompt: The switch that makes Vite's env types strict is the key `___` in the interface `ViteTypeOptions`.
The staging and production builds of one commit have different hashes. What does that mean for a release?

choices.text: One of the two builds is broken
choices.why: Both are correct builds of the same code with different values.

choices.text: What reaches users is not what was checked
choices.why: Right. It is a second build, made later, with other values.

choices.text: The CDN will serve both to every visitor
choices.why: Each environment serves its own build.

choices.text: The hash includes the date, so it always differs
choices.why: Two builds of the same content gave the same hash in lesson 1.

prompt: A team promotes one build from staging to production and keeps per-environment values in a `config.json` fetched at start. Which value must still never go in it?

choices.text: The address of the API for that environment
choices.why: An address is public anyway; this is what the file is for.

choices.text: A title that says which environment it is
choices.why: Harmless; the browser shows it on the page.

choices.text: A key that lets its holder act as the team
choices.why: Right. The file is fetched by the browser, so it is as public as the bundle.

choices.text: The publishable key of an error reporter
choices.why: That one is made to be public.

prompt: In the workflow, which step should receive `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Who needs the token to do their job?

choices.text: The build, so the page can call Cloudflare
choices.why: The page must never hold it.

choices.text: The deploy, which uploads `dist/`
choices.why: Right; only the upload needs it.

choices.text: Every step, through the job's `env:`
choices.why: That would hand it to the build as well.

choices.text: The checkout, to read the repository
choices.why: Checkout uses the workflow's own token.

prompt: A pull request from a fork runs your workflow, and the step needing a secret fails. Why?

choices.text: The fork's branch has no `.env` file
choices.why: Secrets come from the repository's settings, not a file.

choices.text: Secrets expire after each merge
choices.why: They do not expire that way.

choices.text: A fork's pull request gets no secrets
choices.why: Right, so a stranger's code cannot print them.

choices.text: Masking replaced the secret with `***`
choices.why: Masking changes the log, not the value the step receives.

prompt: Which values should a preview build use?

choices.text: Production's, so the preview is realistic
choices.why: A preview is public at its own address; production values do not belong there.

choices.text: Staging's, set per environment at the host
choices.why: Right. That is what per-environment settings are for.

choices.text: None; previews cannot read variables
choices.why: They read them like any build.

choices.text: Whatever is in `.env.local`
choices.why: That file never leaves your machine.

prompt: In the support example, what does the page's bundle contain?

choices.text: The token, encoded so it cannot be read
choices.why: Any encoding the page can undo, a reader can undo.

choices.text: The path `/api/support` and nothing else
choices.why: Right. The token lives in the proxy's environment.

choices.text: The address of the support service
choices.why: Only the proxy talks to the service.

choices.text: Half of the token, the other half on the server
choices.why: Splitting a secret still hands half of it to every reader.

prompt: The proxy is changed to forward any path to the service, adding the key. What has gone wrong?

choices.text: Strangers get every power the key has
choices.why: Right. The proxy should allow the one action the page needs.

choices.text: The key is now visible in the bundle
choices.why: The key is still on the server; the damage is what it can be used for.

choices.text: Nothing; the key is still secret
choices.why: Secret, and usable by anybody through the proxy.

choices.text: The service will refuse requests that come through a proxy
choices.why: It sees a correct key and accepts them.

prompt: What HTTP status did the support service answer without the key?
A secret was pushed to a public repository. Put the response in order.
items: Replace the secret at the service and revoke the old one
Read the service's logs for use of the old one
Remove the file and add it to `.gitignore`
Rewrite the history, if others will clone it

prompt: `git check-ignore -v .env.local .env` prints one line, for `.env.local`. What does that tell you about `.env`?

choices.text: It is ignored by a rule in a global file
choices.why: Then `check-ignore` would have printed that rule.

choices.text: No rule ignores it, so `git add .` would commit it
choices.why: Right. The template expects `.env` to hold shared values.

choices.text: It does not exist
choices.why: `check-ignore` answers about paths whether or not the file exists.

choices.text: It is already committed
choices.why: The command says nothing about what is committed.

prompt: After `git rm --cached .env` and a commit, is the secret gone from the repository?

choices.text: Yes, `--cached` removes it from every commit
choices.why: It removes it from the next commit only.

choices.text: No, the earlier commit still holds it
choices.why: Right. `git log -p -- .env` shows the line.

choices.text: Yes, once `.env` is in `.gitignore`
choices.why: Ignoring affects files not yet tracked, never history.

choices.text: No, but only because it was not pushed
choices.why: Pushed or not, the local history has it.

prompt: GitHub's push protection accepted a push containing your own made-up token format. What does that show?

choices.text: The token was not a secret after all
choices.why: Whether it is a secret is about what it opens, not what a scanner knows.

choices.text: Push protection was turned off
choices.why: It can be on and still not know the format.

choices.text: The scanner knows common formats, not every format
choices.why: Right. It is a net under the rule, never the rule.

choices.text: Private repositories are not scanned
choices.why: The section says nothing of the kind.

prompt: A front end must call a service whose only key is secret. Which design keeps the key secret?

choices.text: `VITE_SERVICE_KEY` set only in the host's dashboard
choices.why: The prefix copies it into the bundle wherever it was set.

choices.text: The key in `config.json`, fetched after sign-in
choices.why: Whatever the browser fetches, the reader has.

choices.text: A small server of yours that holds it and does one action
choices.why: Right: the page calls your server, and only your server holds the key.

choices.text: The key without a prefix, read with `import.meta.env`
choices.why: Then the page gets `undefined` and the feature does not work at all.
